title: SimFlight
description: `hpr sim`: what was flown, from where, and how the flight went.

design.description: The design and the configuration flown.

exports.description: The recording files written, in the order given.

launch.description: The launch site, rail and wind.

notes.description:
What the flight leaves out of the design, such as its parachutes, and what to make of the
numbers it leaves out.

warnings.description:
What the design's or the motor file's reader accepted with a caveat, and what the design's
checks found unusual but buildable.

gain_m.description:
The height gained from where the centre of gravity stood at launch, m, as OpenRocket's
altitude counts.

height_above_ground_m.description: The height above the launch site, m.

DesignConfiguration.description: A motor configuration of the design file.

flies.description: Whether `hpr sim` flies it as the file has it, without `--motor`.

name.description: Its name, as the file writes it; often empty.

oneOf.description: An OpenRocket `.ork` file.
An hpr design file: a `hpr_design::Rocket` as JSON.
The rocket started to move along the rail.
The rocket left the rail.

The highest point.
The centre of mass came down to the launch site's height.
A recovery device's charge fired.
A recovery device deployed.
A recovery device was released.
The stack came apart.
A piece left the airframe at an ejection.
A part started to move along the airframe.
A part left the airframe.
A user event.
A motor lit after launch.
An event this build of `hpr` doesn't name.

rows.description: The rows recorded: one every `--interval` seconds and one at every event.

ExportFormat.description: A recording file's format, from its extension.

oneOf.description: `.csv`: a header of column names with their units, then one line per row.
`.parquet`: Apache Parquet.
`.geojson`: the centre of mass's path on the Earth.
`.kml`: the same path, for Google Earth.
RASP `.eng`.
RockSim `.rse`.

InputWarning.description: Something a reader accepted with a caveat, or the design's checks found unusual.

at.description:
Where: in a `.ork` file, a path of element names from the root or a zip entry's name; in a
motor file, its name and line; `design checks` for a check's finding.

message.description: What was found, and how it was read.

Landing.description:
Where and how fast a body landed: where its centre of mass came down to the launch site's
height on the ellipsoid. There is no terrain.

body.description: The body: `null` for the rocket, or the index of a part that came apart from it.

descent_rate_m_s.description: The rate of descent at the ground, m/s.

distance_m.description: Horizontal distance from the launch site, m.

east_m.description: Distance east of the launch site, m.

ground_hit_speed_m_s.description: The speed at the ground, m/s.

north_m.description: Distance north of the launch site, m.

Launch.description: Where and how the rocket was launched.

atmosphere.description: The atmosphere: always `standard`, the 1976 US Standard Atmosphere.

elevation_m.description: The site's elevation above sea level, m.

heading_deg.description: The direction the rail leans toward, clockwise from true north, degrees.

inclination_deg.description: The rail's angle above the horizon, degrees: 90 is vertical.

rail_length_m.description: The rail's length, m, from the rocket's aft end at the start to the rail's top.

wind_from_deg.description: The direction the wind blows from, clockwise from true north, degrees.

wind_speed_m_s.description: The wind's speed, m/s, the same at every height; 0 for calm air.

Margin.description: A stability margin and what it rests on.

angle_of_attack_rad.description: The total angle of attack, rad.

cp_station_m.description: The centre of pressure, m aft of the nose tip; `null` when the margin is.

margin_cal.description:
The margin, calibres: positive with the centre of pressure aft of the centre of mass;
`null` when the net slope is too small for the quotient to mean anything.

normal_force_slope_per_rad.description: The normal-force slope `C_Nα` on the reference area, per radian.

pitch_moment_slope_per_rad.description: The pitch-moment slope about the centre of mass, per radian; negative restores.

slope_magnitude_sum_per_rad.description: The sum of the parts' slope magnitudes, per radian: the scale the net slope is judged by.

Peak.description: A metric's extreme and when it came.

after_apogee.description:
Whether it came after apogee, in the fall. With no recovery device flown, as `hpr sim`
flies today, a peak in the fall is not a prediction: the fall rests on small-angle
aerodynamics far outside their range.

height_above_ground_m.description: The height above the launch site then, m.

value.description: The value, in the unit the field's name gives.

configuration.description: The id of the motor configuration flown.

configuration_name.description: Its name, as the file writes it; often empty.

configurations.description:
Every motor configuration the file holds, the one flown among them, before `--motor`
changed any.

file.description: The file's name, without its folder.

name.description: The rocket's name, as the file writes it.

height_above_ground_m.description: The centre of gravity's height above the launch site, m.

index.description: The device, part or motor it is about, by its index, for the kinds that have one.

speed_m_s.description: The speed relative to the ground, m/s.

count.description: How many of it fly: one per tube of a cluster, and one per pod of a pod set.

ignition.description: When it lights, in words: `at launch`, or as the design says.

mount.description: The id of the motor mount it is in, which `--mount` takes.

mount_name.description: The mount's name, as the file writes it.

unlit.description: How many of those never light: in a tube the design marks failed, or set never to light.

SimMotorSource.description: Where a flown motor comes from.

oneOf.description: The design file's own configuration.
The bundled catalog, named with `--motor`.
A motor file named with `--motor`.

file.description: The file's name, without its folder.

Stability.description: The rocket's stability at one instant.

cg_station_m.description: The centre of gravity, m aft of the nose tip.

flight_margin.description:
The flight margin: the air along the axis, at the flight's Mach number. The angle of attack
is left out.

height_above_ground_m.description: The height above the launch site, m.

reference_diameter_m.description: The reference diameter the margins are counted in, m.

static_margin.description: The static margin: the air along the axis, at Mach 0.

body_landings.description: Where each part that came apart from the rocket landed, if any did.

landing.description:
Where and how fast the rocket landed. With no recovery device flown, as `hpr sim` flies
today, the fall from apogee rests on small-angle aerodynamics far outside their range: not
a prediction (the notes say so).

launch_height_m.description:
The centre of gravity's height above the launch site at launch, m: not zero, as the rocket
stands on the rail.

max_acceleration_m_s2.description:
The top acceleration of the nose tip relative to the launch site's frame, from liftoff
until a recovery device opens, m/s²: the motion's, not what an accelerometer reads.

max_descent_acceleration_m_s2.description: The top acceleration under the recovery devices, m/s²: the opening shock.

min_flight_margin_cal.description:
The least flight margin, calibres, over the same span: the margin at the flight's Mach
number, along the axis.

min_static_margin_cal.description:
The least static stability margin, calibres, from the rail exit to apogee or the first
deployment.

rail_exit_speed_m_s.description: The speed as the rocket left the rail, m/s.

rail_exit_stability.description: The stability as the rocket left the rail.

oneOf.description: The centre of mass reached the ground.
Every motor burned out before the rocket lifted off.
The rocket lifted off but stopped on the rail after every motor burned out.
The time cap was reached.
The integrator's step limit was reached.
The stack separated, and each part flew on as its own descent.
A way of ending this build of `hpr` doesn't name.
A whole motor had an error and was left out.
A value was dropped or ignored.
Something unusual was read as it stands.
